source: https://aiconference.com/ and https://aiconference.com/dz/ (speakers real; tracks, rooms, and schedule synthesized - agenda unpublished as of 2026-08-31)

tracks.name: AI Frontiers
tracks.description: Research, policy, and frontier-model sessions for researchers, policy leaders, and senior strategists.

tracks.name: AI Builders
tracks.description: Hands-on engineering sessions for software engineers, architects, and tech leads shipping AI products.

tracks.name: The AI Stack
tracks.description: Models, training, and infrastructure sessions for ML researchers, ML/AI engineers, and infrastructure teams.

tracks.name: Applied AI
tracks.description: Production AI in real products, for product managers, applied scientists, and solutions and operations leaders.

tracks.name: AI Strategy
tracks.description: Leadership, investment, and transformation sessions for executives, strategists, and transformation owners.

speakers.name: Peter Norvig
speakers.bio: Peter Norvig is a Distinguished Education Fellow at Stanford's Human-Centered Artificial Intelligence Institute and formerly directed research at Google and NASA's Ames Research Center. He is co-author of Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach, the standard AI textbook.

speakers.name: Emmanuel Ameisen
speakers.bio: Emmanuel Ameisen is an interpretability researcher at Anthropic, working on understanding how large language models work internally. He is the author of Building Machine Learning Powered Applications.

speakers.name: Illia Polosukhin
speakers.bio: Illia Polosukhin is a co-author of the Transformer paper "Attention Is All You Need" and co-founder of NEAR, where he now leads NEAR AI's work on user-owned AI.

speakers.name: Ion Stoica
speakers.bio: Ion Stoica is a professor at UC Berkeley, director of Sky Computing Lab, and co-founder of Databricks and Anyscale. His lab's projects include Spark, Ray, and vLLM.

speakers.name: Chris Lattner
speakers.bio: Chris Lattner is co-founder and CEO of Modular and the creator of LLVM, Clang, Swift, and MLIR. At Modular he leads work on Mojo and a unified AI compute stack.

speakers.name: Brian Yang
speakers.bio: Brian Yang is a Member of Technical Staff at OpenAI, building frontier model products and infrastructure.

speakers.name: Sergey Levine
speakers.bio: Sergey Levine is an associate professor at UC Berkeley and co-founder of Physical Intelligence. His research focuses on reinforcement learning and robot learning at the frontier of embodied AI.

speakers.name: Chris Clark
speakers.bio: Chris Clark is COO and co-founder of OpenRouter, the unified API for accessing and routing across frontier and open AI models.

speakers.name: Eric Ries
speakers.bio: Eric Ries is the author of The Lean Startup and Incorruptible, and founder of the Long-Term Stock Exchange (LTSE).

speakers.name: Tim O'Reilly
speakers.bio: Tim O'Reilly is the founder and CEO of O'Reilly Media and a long-time chronicler of technology platform shifts, from open source to Web 2.0 to AI.

speakers.name: Annie Surla
speakers.bio: Annie Surla is a Product Research Engineering Manager for Deep Learning at NVIDIA, turning deep learning research into developer-facing products and platforms.
speakers.role: Product Research Engineering Manager, Deep Learning

speakers.name: Max Brodeur-Urbas
speakers.bio: Max Brodeur-Urbas is CEO and co-founder of Gumloop, a no-code platform for building AI-powered automations.

speakers.name: Daksh Gupta
speakers.bio: Daksh Gupta is co-founder and CEO of Greptile, which builds AI code review that understands entire codebases.

speakers.name: Ann Miura-Ko
speakers.bio: Ann Miura-Ko is a co-founding partner at Floodgate, a lecturer at Stanford, and one of the earliest backers of thesis-driven seed investing in Silicon Valley.

speakers.name: Jaclyn Konzelmann
speakers.bio: Jaclyn Konzelmann leads AI-first products at Google Labs, including the Gemini API and Google AI Studio.

speakers.name: Marco Paglia
speakers.bio: Marco Paglia leads product and engineering at Musixmatch, the global music data company.

speakers.name: Sarah Chieng
speakers.bio: Sarah Chieng leads Developer Experience at Cerebras, focusing on AI hardware and developer ecosystems, and founded Cafe Compute.

speakers.name: Malika Aubakirova
speakers.bio: Malika Aubakirova is a partner at Andreessen Horowitz investing in AI infrastructure and applications.

speakers.name: Matthew Strozier
speakers.bio: Matthew Strozier is bureau chief of WSJ Pro Venture Capital, covering the venture industry for The Wall Street Journal.

speakers.name: Lauri Moore
speakers.bio: Lauri Moore is a partner at Bessemer Venture Partners, investing in AI, data, and developer platforms.

speakers.name: Jon Sakoda
speakers.bio: Jon Sakoda is the founding partner of Decibel, an early-stage venture firm focused on developer-led and AI-native companies.

speakers.name: Gerrit De Vynck
speakers.bio: Gerrit De Vynck is a technology reporter at The Washington Post covering artificial intelligence and the companies building it.

speakers.name: Rebecca Bauer-Kahan
speakers.bio: Rebecca Bauer-Kahan represents District 16 in the California State Assembly, where she has authored key state legislation on AI and privacy.

speakers.name: Kevin Frazier
speakers.bio: Kevin Frazier is a professor in the AI Innovation & Law Program at the University of Texas School of Law, studying AI governance and regulation.
speakers.company: University of Texas School of Law

speakers.name: Andrew Freedman
speakers.bio: Andrew Freedman is co-founder and CEO of Fathom and previously served as Colorado's first cannabis czar, bringing regulatory experience to AI policy.

speakers.name: Jason Hiner
speakers.bio: Jason Hiner is Chief Content Officer and Editor-in-Chief of The Deep View, covering how AI is transforming business and society.

speakers.name: Claire Southey
speakers.bio: Claire Southey is Chief AI Officer at Rokt, leading AI strategy and applied machine learning across the e-commerce technology company.

speakers.name: Todd Earwood
speakers.bio: Todd Earwood is CEO of Betra Works, helping companies operationalize AI transformation.

speakers.name: Charlie Guo
speakers.bio: Charlie Guo is a Developer Experience Engineer at OpenAI, helping developers build on the OpenAI platform.

speakers.name: Pallavi Kinnera
speakers.bio: Pallavi Kinnera leads AI-driven automation for advanced-node chip design at Meta Reality Labs.

speakers.name: Shuen Mei
speakers.bio: Shuen Mei leads AI, data, and software teams building Harbor Capital Advisors' data, cloud, and integration platforms across financial services.
speakers.role: VP, Director of Software and Data Engineering

speakers.name: Pratyusha Singaraju
speakers.bio: Pratyusha Singaraju designs and builds AI-powered backend services driving content understanding for Netflix search and discovery.

speakers.name: Julia Diament

speakers.role: Principal AI Architect, Office of the CTO

speakers.name: Divya Mahajan
speakers.bio: Divya Mahajan builds production-grade agentic AI and LLM systems at Alexa scale, leading evaluation and multi-turn workflows for Alexa+ users.

speakers.name: Ran Li
speakers.bio: Ran Li is a technical lead at Google working on AI-powered products at global scale.

speakers.name: Vidya Meenakshi
speakers.bio: Vidya Meenakshi builds backend experimentation platforms at Intuit, including the Experimentation Agent and MCP server.

speakers.name: Ioannis Antonoglou

speakers.name: Jon Pappas
speakers.bio: Jon Pappas leads AI-powered talent search, matching, and deployment at Upwork.
speakers.role: Sr. Director of Technical Product Management

speakers.name: Yogiraj Awati
speakers.bio: Yogiraj Awati leads large-scale AI and RAG platforms powering Instacart's grocery experience.

speakers.name: Ryan Lopopolo
speakers.bio: Ryan Lopopolo builds agent-first development workflows at OpenAI, authoring the Harness Engineering framework.

speakers.name: Ruiyang Wang
speakers.bio: Ruiyang Wang builds infrastructure and data systems behind Anthropic's large language models, previously at Anyscale and Google Cloud.

speakers.name: Lisa Shen
speakers.bio: Lisa Shen is a Product Manager at Google Cloud working on Cloud Run and serverless AI infrastructure.

speakers.name: João Moura
speakers.bio: João Moura is the creator of CrewAI and CEO of crewAI, building frameworks and platforms for orchestrating multi-agent AI systems.

speakers.name: Lorenze Hay
speakers.bio: Lorenze Hay is a software engineer at crewAI working on production agent orchestration.

speakers.name: Milin Desai
speakers.bio: Milin Desai currently serves as the CEO of Sentry. Used by more than 4 million developers and 150,000 organizations worldwide, Sentry helps every developer detect, understand, and fix broken code, fast.

talks.title: Building Production-Ready AI Agents on Google Cloud Run
talks.description: Prototyping an AI agent is faster than ever, but transitioning that prototype into a secure, scalable, and observable production application is where the real engineering begins. In this 90-minute interactive workshop, you will move beyond Day 1 demos to master enterprise-grade AI deployment on Google Cloud's serverless platform, with hands-on labs for agents and serverless-GPU inference on Cloud Run.

talks.title: Designing Agentic Systems
talks.description: Most agents don't fail in production because the model is bad. They fail because the system around the model has no guardrails, no structure, and no way to see what's happening. This session walks through the harness every production agent needs: control flow, a real plan-execute-observe-replan design, and observability you can act on, backed by a benchmark where the same model went from 20% to 60%+ just by changing the system. You'll leave with a pre-deploy checklist.

talks.title: Hands-On LLM Interpretability
talks.description: A hands-on introduction to interpretability for practitioners. Trace circuits and features in open models, see how interpretability tooling explains model behavior, and learn what current techniques can and cannot tell you about the systems you deploy.

talks.title: Fast Inference, Hands-On: Building on Wafer-Scale Compute
talks.description: Build and benchmark applications against ultra-low-latency inference APIs. This workshop covers when inference speed changes product design, how to structure agentic workloads around fast token generation, and hands-on exercises with wafer-scale inference endpoints.

talks.title: The Lean AI Startup
talks.description: Eric Ries applies the Lean Startup method to AI-era company building: how to run honest experiments when demos are cheap and reliability is expensive, what validated learning looks like for AI products, and how to keep a startup incorruptible while it scales.

talks.title: Standing Up an Enterprise AI Function
talks.description: A working session for executives building an AI organization: operating models for a Chief AI Officer, choosing the first production use cases, measuring impact, and avoiding the pilot-purgatory trap.

talks.title: Secure-by-Design AI: A Governance Workshop
talks.description: Translate AI governance from policy documents into engineering practice. Covers adversarial threat modeling for LLM applications, secure-by-design patterns, and a governance checklist you can apply to systems already in production.

talks.title: Fundraising Readiness for AI Founders
talks.description: What top-tier investors actually evaluate in AI startups: moats beyond the model, margin structure under inference costs, and how to present traction. Includes working sessions on positioning and common diligence failure modes.

talks.title: What Everyone Should Know About AI
talks.description: Peter Norvig on the state of artificial intelligence in 2026: what the textbook view gets right, what frontier models changed, and how education must adapt so the next generation can build with, and reason about, AI.

talks.title: Democratizing AI Compute
talks.description: Chris Lattner on breaking the hardware lock-in holding AI back: lessons from LLVM, Swift, and MLIR applied to Mojo and Modular's unified compute stack, and why the next wave of AI progress depends on programmable, portable performance.

talks.title: Systems for AI: From Spark to vLLM and Beyond
talks.description: Ion Stoica traces the systems lineage behind today's AI boom, from Spark and Ray to vLLM and Sky Computing, and lays out the open infrastructure problems that will define the next five years of AI systems research.

talks.title: From AlphaGo to Superintelligence: Lessons in RL
talks.description: A core architect of AlphaGo, AlphaZero, and MuZero on what reinforcement learning taught us about building agents that exceed human performance, and how those lessons drive Reflection AI's pursuit of superintelligent autonomous systems.

talks.title: Thesis-Driven Investing in the AI Wave
talks.description: Floodgate's co-founding partner on separating durable AI companies from demos: the theses that survive hype cycles, what founders misread about defensibility, and where the biggest under-hyped opportunities sit.

talks.title: From Transformers to User-Owned AI
talks.description: A co-author of "Attention Is All You Need" on the arc from the Transformer to today's frontier, and why the next chapter should be user-owned: open models, verifiable inference, and AI that works for the people using it.

talks.title: Foundation Models for the Physical World
talks.description: Sergey Levine on robot learning at the foundation-model moment: what it takes to bring the scaling recipe to embodied agents, and what robots reveal about the limits of internet-trained intelligence.

talks.title: AI and the Next Economy
talks.description: Tim O'Reilly on the platform shift underway: what previous transitions teach us about who captures value, why disclosure and interoperability matter, and how to build an AI economy that creates more value than it captures.

talks.title: Building AI Companies That Matter
talks.description: Eric Ries on company building in the AI era: applying validated learning when everything demos well, governance structures that keep companies incorruptible, and what long-term thinking looks like amid the fastest technology cycle ever.

talks.title: Fundraising & the Future of AI Companies
talks.description: WSJ Pro Venture Capital bureau chief Matthew Strozier moderates a panel of leading investors on the state of AI fundraising: round dynamics, what diligence looks like when everyone claims AI, and where venture returns will actually come from.

talks.title: The State of AI Regulation
talks.description: Washington Post tech reporter Gerrit De Vynck moderates California Assemblymember Rebecca Bauer-Kahan, law professor Kevin Frazier, and Fathom CEO Andrew Freedman on where AI regulation stands, what state and federal rules are coming, and what builders should prepare for.

talks.title: What AI Transformation Actually Looks Like
talks.description: The Deep View's Jason Hiner moderates Rokt Chief AI Officer Claire Southey and Betra Works CEO Todd Earwood on real enterprise AI transformation: what worked, what stalled, and how to measure impact beyond the pilot.

talks.title: Developer Experience for the Agent Era
talks.description: OpenAI's Charlie Guo on what changes when your API users are agents as much as humans: designing SDKs, docs, and tooling for the agentic development loop on the OpenAI platform.

talks.title: What a Million AI Code Reviews Taught Us
talks.description: Greptile's CEO on running AI code review across massive codebases: where models catch what humans miss, where they still fail, and how full-codebase context changes the review game.

talks.title: No-Code Agents That Actually Ship
talks.description: Gumloop's CEO on what thousands of production automations reveal about which agent workflows deliver value, and how no-code changes who gets to build with AI.

talks.title: Debugging AI Applications in Production with Sentry
talks.description: AI features fail in ways traditional monitoring never sees: bad completions, runaway token spend, silent tool-call errors. Sentry CEO Milin Desai shows how to instrument LLM applications end to end - tracing model calls, surfacing agent failures, and connecting AI errors to the code that caused them - so you can detect, understand, and fix broken AI code fast.

talks.title: Harness Engineering: Agent-First Development
talks.description: The author of OpenAI's Harness Engineering framework on restructuring development workflows around agents: harness design, guardrails, and what changes when agents write most of the code.

talks.title: Routing the World's Inference
talks.description: OpenRouter's co-founder on what aggregate traffic across hundreds of models says about the AI market: model selection in practice, fallback and routing strategies, and the economics of inference.

talks.title: Shipping Products on Frontier Models
talks.description: An OpenAI Member of Technical Staff on the gap between a capable model and a shippable product: evaluation, latency budgets, and the engineering under frontier-model features.

talks.title: An Experimentation Agent and MCP Server at Intuit
talks.description: How Intuit built an Experimentation Agent and MCP server on its backend experimentation platform, letting AI assistants design, launch, and analyze experiments safely.

talks.title: Inside the Mind of a Language Model
talks.description: An Anthropic interpretability researcher on what we now know about how LLMs work internally: circuits, features, and what interpretability findings mean for the systems you deploy.

talks.title: Data Infrastructure Behind Frontier Models
talks.description: An Anthropic Member of Technical Staff on the data systems behind large-model training: pipelines at petabyte scale, quality over quantity, and infrastructure lessons from Anyscale and Google Cloud.

talks.title: From Research Paper to Developer Platform
talks.description: NVIDIA's deep learning product research lens on turning research advances into developer products: what survives contact with production, and how research and product teams should collaborate.

talks.title: When Inference Is Instant
talks.description: Cerebras' Head of Developer Experience on what wafer-scale inference speed unlocks for developers: agentic workloads, reasoning at interactive latency, and building an ecosystem around fast tokens.

talks.title: AI Designing the Chips That Run AI
talks.description: Inside AI-driven automation for advanced-node chip design at Meta Reality Labs: where ML accelerates physical design today and what it means for the hardware feedback loop.

talks.title: RAG at Grocery Scale
talks.description: Instacart's engineering lead on large-scale AI and RAG platforms behind the grocery experience: retrieval over messy catalog data, latency budgets, and measuring answer quality in production.

talks.title: Content Understanding for Search and Discovery
talks.description: A Netflix senior engineer on AI-powered backend services for content understanding: how embeddings and LLMs reshape search and discovery for a global catalog.

talks.title: Evaluating Multi-Turn Agents at Alexa Scale
talks.description: Building production-grade agentic AI at Alexa scale: evaluation harnesses for multi-turn workflows, catching regressions before users do, and operating LLM systems for millions of Alexa+ users.

talks.title: Building Gemini API and Google AI Studio
talks.description: Google Labs' product director on making frontier models buildable: product lessons from the Gemini API and AI Studio, and what developers actually need from an AI platform.

talks.title: Shipping AI Features at Google Scale
talks.description: A Google technical lead on taking AI features from prototype to billions of users: rollout strategy, quality bars, and the organizational mechanics of shipping AI at scale.

talks.title: AI-Powered Talent Matching at Upwork
talks.description: Upwork's product lead on AI-powered talent search, matching, and deployment: ranking humans instead of documents, and how agents change the future of work marketplaces.

talks.title: Music Data Meets AI
talks.description: Musixmatch's president of product and engineering on AI over the world's largest lyrics dataset: licensing-aware ML, music understanding, and product bets at the intersection of AI and music.

talks.title: Adversarial Threats to AI Systems
talks.description: A principal AI architect in Microsoft's Office of the CTO on the adversarial threat landscape for deployed AI: prompt injection, data poisoning, model theft, and the secure-by-design patterns that counter them.

talks.title: AI and Data Platforms in Financial Services
talks.description: Harbor Capital Advisors' VP of software and data engineering on building AI, data, cloud, and integration platforms in a regulated industry, and where AI genuinely moves the needle in finance.

talks.title: What Durable AI Companies Look Like
talks.description: An Andreessen Horowitz partner on the patterns behind AI startups that endure: moats beyond the model, the shape of AI-native business models, and what the next funding cycle rewards.
